messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy: design notes

Working notes for Quizzy. Keep them current when the behaviour changes.

## Scope

- Moderator area under `/moderate`, HTTP Basic (`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`).
- Quizzes, single-choice questions with text options, the "Active" switch, move up/down,
  delete, and the preview (a player's walk-through, nothing stored).
- Export and import of a quiz as JSON: "Export" on the quiz page, "Import quiz" on the quiz list.
- The live game: "Start a game" opens a game on the big screen (`/moderate/games/:id`). Phones join
  at `/play/:code` with no account. Everything follows the game live. See "Live game" below.
- Not built yet: leaderboards and scores over time (the stylesheet has classes for them:
  `leader*`, `winner-banner`, `response-*`).

## Running

- `bin/serve` is the only entry point used in production. It needs `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and the two
  moderator variables (it stops with a message if one is missing), runs `bin/rails db:prepare`,
  and starts Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.
- Data: `storage/production.sqlite3` (app), plus `production_cache|queue|cable.sqlite3` from the
  default Solid* setup. Nothing else is written under `storage/`.
- HTTP only: `force_ssl` and `assume_ssl` are off; host authorization is not configured, so any
  host name is accepted. `/up` is Rails' health check (200 when booted).
- Assets: Propshaft serves `app/assets` itself in production (`config.assets.server = true`),
  because there is no proxy in front and no asset precompile step. `quizzy.css` and the font
  come from the design unchanged, apart from the font path. `moderator.css` holds app additions.
- No external calls. Turbo, Stimulus and importmap are vendored by their gems and served locally.
- The QR code is drawn on the server (`rqrcode`, gem installed locally): no QR service is called.
- Live pages poll a fragment every 2-3 seconds. `config/environments/production.rb` keeps those
  requests out of the log (`SilenceRequest` on the `/live` paths), as it does `/up`.

## Routes

| Page | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiz list | `GET /moderate` | "New quiz" is a GET button to the form |
| New quiz / save | `GET/POST /moderate/quizzes(/new)` | Saving opens the quiz page |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` | "Add question" (GET button), "Settings", "Preview" |
| Settings | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | Same form as new; "Delete quiz" with confirm |
| Export | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | Quiz as JSON in the only `<pre>`; "Export" link on the quiz page |
| Import form | `GET /moderate/imports/new` | "Import quiz" (GET button) on the quiz list; "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" button |
| Import | `POST /moderate/imports` | Always a new quiz; redirects to it (303). Errors: 422, nothing saved |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | State lives in the query string (see below) |
| New question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new` | Form, four empty rows, Active on |
| Create question | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions` | Also handles "Add option" (no save) |
| Edit question | `GET /moderate/questions/:id/edit` | |
| Update / delete | `PATCH/DELETE /moderate/questions/:id` | Delete asks with `confirm()` |
| Move | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/move_up` and `/move_down` | Swaps with the neighbour in list order |
| Active switch | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/activation` | Form submits on change (Stimulus `auto-submit`) |
| Start a game | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games` | A new game of the quiz; redirects to its big screen (303) |
| Big screen | `GET /moderate/games/:id` | Layout `screen`. The live region is the whole screen, controls included |
| Big screen state | `GET /moderate/games/:id/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304 when nothing changed) |
| Step | `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `/finish`, `/next_question`, `/end_quiz` | Each step is refused (flash, nothing changes) when the phase does not allow it |
| Join page | `GET /play/:code` | Name form, then the phone's state. Unknown code: 404. Code is case-insensitive |
| Phone state | `GET /play/:code/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304) |
| Join | `POST /play/:code/join` | Sets the player cookie; a second join from the same browser changes nothing |
| Answer | `POST /play/:code/answers` (`option_id`) | The last pick counts; refused unless the question is open |

## Data

- `quizzes(title)`, `questions(quiz_id, text, position, active)`, `options(question_id, text, correct, position)`.
- Positions are unique per quiz and only swapped, never renumbered. A new question gets `max + 1`.
- Deleting a quiz or question deletes its options (dependent destroy). Deleting a quiz also deletes
  its games.
- Games (see "Live game"): `games(quiz_id, code, phase, current_position, revision, finished_at)`,
  `game_questions(game_id, position, text, opened_at, closed_at)`, `game_options(game_question_id,
  position, text, correct)`, `players(game_id,",
  "output_tail": " the game's join link.

## Test it

```sh
bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
bin/rails test:system   # browser tests on the local Chromium (Cuprite, no chromedriver)
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman -q
```

The app and its tests run without network access: gems are installed locally and the
stylesheet, font and JavaScript are served from the repository.

## Docs

- `docs/notes.md`: design notes, routes, data rules, the live game, and decisions.
- `docs/mockups/`: the design's style guide and the screens of the moderator side.

# Quizzy: design notes

Working notes for Quizzy. Keep them current when the behaviour changes.

## Scope

- Moderator area under `/moderate`, HTTP Basic (`QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`).
- Quizzes, single-choice questions with text options, the "Active" switch, move up/down,
  delete, and the preview (a player's walk-through, nothing stored).
- Export and import of a quiz as JSON: "Export" on the quiz page, "Import quiz" on the quiz list.
- The live game: "Start a game" opens a game on the big screen (`/moderate/games/:id`). Phones join
  at `/play/:code` with no account. Everything follows the game live. See "Live game" below.
- Not built yet: leaderboards and scores over time (the stylesheet has classes for them:
  `leader*`, `winner-banner`, `response-*`).

## Running

- `bin/serve` is the only entry point used in production. It needs `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and the two
  moderator variables (it stops with a message if one is missing), runs `bin/rails db:prepare`,
  and starts Puma on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.
- Data: `storage/production.sqlite3` (app), plus `production_cache|queue|cable.sqlite3` from the
  default Solid* setup. Nothing else is written under `storage/`.
- HTTP only: `force_ssl` and `assume_ssl` are off; host authorization is not configured, so any
  host name is accepted. `/up` is Rails' health check (200 when booted).
- Assets: Propshaft serves `app/assets` itself in production (`config.assets.server = true`),
  because there is no proxy in front and no asset precompile step. `quizzy.css` and the font
  come from the design unchanged, apart from the font path. `moderator.css` holds app additions.
- No external calls. Turbo, Stimulus and importmap are vendored by their gems and served locally.
- The QR code is drawn on the server (`rqrcode`, gem installed locally): no QR service is called.
- Live pages poll a fragment every 2-3 seconds. `config/environments/production.rb` keeps those
  requests out of the log (`SilenceRequest` on the `/live` paths), as it does `/up`.

## Routes

| Page | Route | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiz list | `GET /moderate` | "New quiz" is a GET button to the form |
| New quiz / save | `GET/POST /moderate/quizzes(/new)` | Saving opens the quiz page |
| Quiz page | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id` | "Add question" (GET button), "Settings", "Preview" |
| Settings | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | Same form as new; "Delete quiz" with confirm |
| Export | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | Quiz as JSON in the only `<pre>`; "Export" link on the quiz page |
| Import form | `GET /moderate/imports/new` | "Import quiz" (GET button) on the quiz list; "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" button |
| Import | `POST /moderate/imports` | Always a new quiz; redirects to it (303). Errors: 422, nothing saved |
| Preview | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | State lives in the query string (see below) |
| New question | `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions/new` | Form, four empty rows, Active on |
| Create question | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/questions` | Also handles "Add option" (no save) |
| Edit question | `GET /moderate/questions/:id/edit` | |
| Update / delete | `PATCH/DELETE /moderate/questions/:id` | Delete asks with `confirm()` |
| Move | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/move_up` and `/move_down` | Swaps with the neighbour in list order |
| Active switch | `PATCH /moderate/questions/:id/activation` | Form submits on change (Stimulus `auto-submit`) |
| Start a game | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games` | A new game of the quiz; redirects to its big screen (303) |
| Big screen | `GET /moderate/games/:id` | Layout `screen`. The live region is the whole screen, controls included |
| Big screen state | `GET /moderate/games/:id/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304 when nothing changed) |
| Step | `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `/finish`, `/next_question`, `/end_quiz` | Each step is refused (flash, nothing changes) when the phase does not allow it |
| Join page | `GET /play/:code` | Name form, then the phone's state. Unknown code: 404. Code is case-insensitive |
| Phone state | `GET /play/:code/live` | Fragment for polls (ETag, 304) |
| Join | `POST /play/:code/join` | Sets the player cookie; a second join from the same browser changes nothing |
| Answer | `POST /play/:code/answers` (`option_id`) | The last pick counts; refused unless the question is open |

  position, text, correct)`, `players(game_id,

## Test it

```sh
bin/rails test          # models and integration tests
bin/rails test:system   # browser tests on the local Chromium (Cuprite, no chromedriver)
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman -q
```

The app and its tests run without network access: gems are installed locally and the
stylesheet, font and JavaScript are served from the repository.

## Docs

- `docs/notes.md`: design notes, routes, data rules, the live game, and decisions.
- `docs/mockups/`: the design's style guide and the screens of the moderator side.

re-rendered with 422 and exactly what was typed. The options are replaced inside the question's
save transaction, so the stored options never change on a failed save. "Active" alone saves
without touching options (`option_rows` is not assigned, so the rules do not run).

## Form details

- Option rows are named `question[options][i][text]` / `[correct]`. Labels: a visually hidden
  "Option N" for the text field (placeholder "Option text"), and a visible "Option N is correct"
  next to the checkbox. Both are real `<label>`s, so QA can find them by label text.
- "Add option" is a submit button with `formnovalidate`, `name=add_option`. The controller adds one
  empty row and re-renders with 200. Nothing is saved.
- Enter in an option field would submit through the first submit button in DOM order. A hidden
  `<button>` with no text comes first in the form, so Enter saves (tested in the system tests).
- The question form has `data-turbo="false"`: it re-renders with plain HTML responses.
- Edit shows the stored options plus empty rows, padded to four rows, like a new question.

## Live game

### Game = a snapshot

- `Game.create_from_quiz!` copies the quiz's **active** questions, in quiz order, with their options
  and correct flags. Inactive questions are left out, so a game skips them. The game never reads the
  quiz again: editing or deleting questions changes neither a running game nor a past one.
- Each start of "Start a game" is a new game with its own code, players and answers. Rehearsals and
  the real talk do not share anything.
- Join codes: 5 characters from `Game::CODE_ALPHABET` (no 0, O, 1, I, L), unique.

### Phases

| Phase | Meaning | Moderator's button | Phones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lobby` | Players join, nothing is open | "Start" (or "End quiz" when no question is active) | "Hi, <name>!" and waiting |
| `open` | The current question takes answers | "Finish" | Options as buttons, "Your answer" on the pick |
| `closed` | The question is closed, results shown | "Next", or "End quiz" on the last question | "Correct!", "Wrong!" or "No answer", the right option marked |
| `finished` | Over: no joins, no answers | (none, "Back to quiz") | "The quiz is over", the player's score |

- "End quiz" works from any phase. An open question is closed by it.
- Every step is a transition under `with_lock`. A step the phase does not allow returns false and
  changes nothing (no revision bump, no broadcast). The screen then shows a flash with the reason.
- `revision` goes up on every phase change. It is part of the ETags, so phones and screens notice.

### Counters and what they count

- Lobby: "Players: N" counts every player who joined this game.
- "Answers: x / y" (open and closed): `x` = players who answered the current question, `y` = all
  players in the game, including those who joined after the question opened.
- Scores: a player's score counts correct picks on closed questions. The end page shows
  "Your score: x of y" where `y` is the number of closed questions.

### The rule: no correct answer before the question is closed

- The phone's open-question markup has no `correct` flag, no `is-correct` class, no hint text. The
  options are buttons whose `value` is the option id. Tests check the HTML for "correct" (case
  insensitive) and for `is-correct`, `data-correct`, "Right answer" during the open phase.
- The big screen's open markup has no counts and no marks. Counts and the "Correct" marks come
  only in `closed`.
- Pokes (below) carry no data. The fingerprints (ETags) are numbers and ids, no answers. So no
  stream and no ETag ever reveals a correct answer early.
- A phone only ever gets its own player's state (the token is in its cookie).

### Who is the player

- Joining creates a `Player` with a random token (`SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)`).
- The token goes into a permanent, encrypted, httponly cookie named `quizzy_player_<CODE>`, one per
  game. Opening the join link again from that browser finds the player and continues. Another
  browser is another player, even with the same name.
- A finished game refuses joins. Its join link shows "The quiz is over" to everyone.

### Live updates

Two mechanisms, both without page reloads. They cover each other's gaps, which matters on crowded
Wi-Fi (missed messages, sleeping phones, dropped sockets):

1. **Pokes (push).** After a change the server broadcasts a Turbo stream with the custom action
   `quizzy_refresh` (`Game#announce`). Two streams per game: `[game, :screen]` for the big screen,
   `[game, :players]` for phones. Phase changes poke both. Joins and answers poke the screen only,
   so 200 phones answering do not make 200 phones reload. `app/javascript/application.js` registers
   the action; it dispatches a `quizzy:refresh` window event with no data.
2. **Polls (pull).** Every live region (`live` Stimulus controller, `app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
   asks its `live` fragment every 2 s (screen) or 3 s (phone). The fragment carries an ETag over the
   state it shows (`LiveRegion`, `Game#screen_fingerprint`, `Game#player_fingerprint`). Nothing new
   means `304` and no DOM work. Polls also run on `visibilitychange` (phone back in front) and `online`.

Client details that matter:

- A poke refresh waits a random 0-400 ms, so the room does not ask all at once. A refresh that is
  already in flight is followed by one more, never more than that.
- Responses are numbered; an older response never overwrites a newer one.
- The region is replaced as a whole (`innerHTML`). Text typed in the region is kept, and focus is
  put back (the name field of the join form must survive a refresh).
"

- The phone's open-question markup has no `correct` flag, no `is-correct` class, no hint text. The
  options are buttons whose `value` is the option id. Tests check the HTML for "correct" (case
  insensitive) and for `is-correct`, `data-correct`, "Right answer" during the open phase.
- The big screen's open markup has no counts and no marks. Counts and the "Correct" marks come
  only in `closed`.
- Pokes (below) carry no data. The fingerprints (ETags) are numbers and ids, no answers. So no
  stream and no ETag ever reveals a correct answer early.
- A phone only ever gets its own player's state (the token is in its cookie).

### Who is the player

- Joining creates a `Player` with a random token (`SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)`).
- The token goes into a permanent, encrypted, httponly cookie named `quizzy_player_<CODE>`, one per
  game. Opening the join link again from that browser finds the player and continues. Another
  browser is another player, even with the same name.
- A finished game refuses joins. Its join link shows "The quiz is over" to everyone.

### Live updates

Two mechanisms, both without page reloads. They cover each other's gaps, which matters on crowded
Wi-Fi (missed messages, sleeping phones, dropped sockets):

1. **Pokes (push).** After a change the server broadcasts a Turbo stream with the custom action
   `quizzy_refresh` (`Game#announce`). Two streams per game: `[game, :screen]` for the big screen,
   `[game, :players]` for phones. Phase changes poke both. Joins and answers poke the screen only,
   so 200 phones answering do not make 200 phones reload. `app/javascript/application.js` registers
   the action; it dispatches a `quizzy:refresh` window event with no data.
2. **Polls (pull).** Every live region (`live` Stimulus controller, `app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
   asks its `live` fragment every 2 s (screen) or 3 s (phone). The fragment carries an ETag over the
   state it shows (`LiveRegion`, `Game#screen_fingerprint`, `Game#player_fingerprint`). Nothing new
   means `304` and no DOM work. Polls also run on `visibilitychange` (phone back in front) and `online`.

Client details that matter:

- A poke refresh waits a random 0-400 ms, so the room does not ask all at once. A refresh that is
  already in flight is followed by one more, never more than that.
- Responses are numbered; an older response never overwrites a newer one.
- The region is replaced as a whole (`innerHTML`). Text typed in the region is kept, and focus is
  put back (the name field of the join form must survive a refresh).

  with the same title exists. On success it redirects to the new quiz with "Quiz imported.".
- Lenient on purpose: `active` defaults to true, `correct` to false, and a `null` counts as missing.
  Keys outside the format are ignored. A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start is skipped.

  option rows with blank text are dropped (their correct box too), at least two filled options, at

  reported, and the rule checks are skipped while any exist, so a bad value does not also show
  misleading rule errors such as "Add at least two options".

  every question, so all broken questions are reported), then saved in one transaction. Any error: 422, "Nothing was
  imported.", the pasted text stays in the text area, and no quiz, question or option is written.

messages.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# One run of a quiz. The game keeps its own copy of the quiz's active questions and their options
# (see `create_from_quiz!`), so editing or deactivating questions never changes a game that is
# running or was played.
#
# Phases:
#   lobby    players join, nothing is open yet
#   open     the current question takes answers
#   closed   the current question is closed and its results are shown
#   finished the game is over: no more joins, no more answers
#
# Every phase change bumps `revision`, and tells the screens and phones to reload (see `announce`).
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[ lobby open closed finished ].freeze
  # Join codes avoid look-alike characters (no 0, O, 1, I, L), so they can be read out loud.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[ 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z ].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, length: { is: CODE_LENGTH }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :revision, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Copies the quiz's active questions, in quiz order, with their options. Inactive questions
  # are left out, so a game skips them.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz)
      quiz.active_questions.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(text: question.text, position: position)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.game_options.create!(text: option.text, correct: option.correct?, position: option_position)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def finished? = phase == "finished"

  def question_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return if current_position.nil?

    game_questions.find_by(position: current_position)
  end

  # Questions that were closed, in order: the ones a player's score is counted over.
  def played_question_count
    game_questions.where.not(closed_at: nil).count
  end

  # Moderator transitions. Each returns true when it changed the game, false when the phase did
  # not allow it (for example, a second click on "Next").
  def start!
    transition do
      next false unless lobby? && game_questions.exists?

      open_question_at!(1)
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    transition do
      next false unless open?

      close_current_question!
      update!(phase: "closed")
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    transition do
      next false unless closed? && current_position < question_count

      open_question_at!(current_position + 1)
    end
  end

  # Ends the game from any phase before "finished". A question that is still open is closed too.
  def end_quiz!
    transition do
      next false if finished?

      close_current_question! if open?
      update!(phase: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)

# One run of a quiz. The game keeps its own copy of the quiz's active questions and their options
# (see `create_from_quiz!`), so editing or deactivating questions never changes a game that is
# running or was played.
#
# Phases:
#   lobby    players join, nothing is open yet
#   open     the current question takes answers
#   closed   the current question is closed and its results are shown
#   finished the game is over: no more joins, no more answers
#
# Every phase change bumps `revision`, and tells the screens and phones to reload (see `announce`).

  # Join codes avoid look-alike characters (no 0, O, 1, I, L), so they can be read out loud.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[ 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z ].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  # Copies the quiz's active questions, in quiz order, with their options. Inactive questions
  # are left out, so a game skips them.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz)
      quiz.active_questions.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(text: question.text, position: position)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.game_options.create!(text: option.text, correct: option.correct?, position: option_position)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def finished? = phase == "finished"

# A live page keeps one region up to date by polling a fragment of itself. Each fragment carries an
# ETag over the state it shows, so a poll that finds nothing new gets a 304 and no HTML.
module LiveRegion
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  def live_etag(parts)
    %(W/"#{Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(Array(parts).join("|"))[0, 32]}")
  end

  def render_live_fragment(etag)
    response.set_header("ETag", etag)
    response.set_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache, private")
    if request.headers["If-None-Match"].to_s.split(",").map(&:strip).include?(etag)
      head :not_modified
    else
      render :live, layout: false
    end
  end
end
module Moderate
  # Everything under /moderate needs the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.
  class BaseController < ApplicationController
    REALM = "Quizzy moderator".freeze

    before_action :authenticate_moderator!

    private

    def authenticate_moderator!
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic(REALM) do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    # Fails closed: if the configured credentials are missing, nobody gets in.
    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      username_matches = ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username)
      password_matches = ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password.to_s, expected_password)
      username_matches && password_matches
    end
  end
end

  "output": "# The phone side of a game: the join page, the answer buttons, and the live state a phone follows.
class PlayController < ApplicationController
  include LiveRegion

  layout "play"

  ANSWER_REFUSALS = {
    not_joined: "Join the quiz first.",
    closed: "This question is closed.",
    unknown_option: "That question is no longer open."
  }.freeze

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :set_player
  before_action :set_live_etag

  def show
  end

  def live
    render_live_fragment(@live_etag)
  end

  def join
    return redirect_to(play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other) if @player || @game.finished?

    player = @game.join(params[:name].to_s)
    if player.persisted?
      cookies.permanent.encrypted[player_cookie_name] = { value: player.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      @join = player
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def answer
    result = @player ? @game.record_answer(@player, params[:option_id]) : :not_joined
    flash[:alert] = ANSWER_REFUSALS.fetch(result, "Your answer was not saved.") unless result == :recorded
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  # The browser that joined keeps its player's token, one cookie per game.
  def set_player
    token = cookies.encrypted[player_cookie_name]
    @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
  end

  def set_live_etag
    @live_etag = live_etag(@game.player_fingerprint(@player))
  end

  def player_cookie_name
    "quizzy_player_#{@game.code}"
  end
end

class PlayController < ApplicationController

  end

# Creates a new quiz, with its questions and options, from JSON in the export format:
#
#   { "title": "...", "questions": [ { "text": "...", "active": true,
#       "options": [ { "text": "...", "correct": false } ] } ] }
#
# `active` defaults to true and `correct` to false. Questions and options keep their order.
# Every question follows the rules of the question form (Question model). The whole document is
# checked before anything is written: when a rule breaks, nothing is saved, not the quiz and not
# any of its questions.
class QuizImport
  include ActiveModel::Validations

  attr_reader :quiz

  validate :read_document

  def initialize(json_text)
    @json_text = json_text.to_s
    @quiz = nil
    @questions = []
    @imported = false
  end

  # Returns true when the quiz and all its questions are saved. Saving again does not import twice.
  def save
    return true if @imported
    return false unless valid?

    Quiz.transaction do
      quiz.save!
      @questions.each { |question, _label| question.save! }
    end
    @imported = true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    errors.add(:base, error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    false
  end

  private

  # Runs on every validation, so it starts from nothing: records are never built twice.
  def read_document
    @quiz = nil
    @questions = []

    document = parse_json
    return if errors.any?

    unless document.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON must be an object with a title and a list of questions")
      return
    end

    @quiz = Quiz.new(title: string_value(document["title"], "Title"))
    questions = document.fetch("questions", nil)
    unless questions.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON needs a list of questions")
      return
    end

    questions.each_with_index { |raw, index| build_question(raw, index + 1) }
    # Format errors come first: the rule checks would only repeat them as misleading rule errors.
    check_records unless errors.any?
  end

  def parse_json
    unless @json_text.valid_encoding?
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON")
      return
    end

    text = @json_text.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").strip
    if text.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Paste the quiz JSON to import")
      return
    end

    JSON.parse(text)
  rescue JSON::ParserError
    errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON is not valid JSON")
    nil
  end

  def build_question(raw, number)
    label = "Question #{number}"
    unless raw.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be an object")
      return
    end

    question = Question.new(
      quiz: quiz,
      text: string_value(raw["text"], "#{label}: text"),
      active: boolean_value(raw["active"], true, "#{label}: active"),
      position: number
    )
    question.option_rows = option_rows(raw["options"], label)
    @questions << [ question, label ]
  end

  def option_rows(raw_options, label)
    return [] if raw_options.nil?

    unless raw_options.is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "#{label}: options must be a list")
      return []
    end

    raw_options.each_with_index.map do |raw, index|
      option_label = "#{label}: option #{index + 1}"
      unless raw.is_a?(Hash)
        errors.add(:base, "#{option_label} must be an object")
        next { text: "", correct: false }
      end

      {
        text: string_value(raw["text"], "#{option_label} text"),
        correct: boolean_value(raw["correct"], false, "#{option_label} correct")
      }
    end
  end

  # Runs the model rules on the quiz and on each question. Question errors carry the question's number.
  def check_records
    copy_errors(quiz, nil)
    @questions.each { |question, label| copy_errors(question, label) }
  end

  def copy_errors(record, label)
    return if record.valid?

    record.errors.full_messages.each do |message|
      errors.add(:base, label ? "#{label}: #{message}" : message)
    end
  end

  # A missing or null value is an empty string, which the model then rejects where text is required.
  def string_value(value, label)
    return "" if value.nil?
    return value if value.is_a?(String)

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be a string")
    ""
  end

  # A missing or null value takes the default; anything other than true or false is an error.
  def boolean_value(value, default, label)
    return default if value.nil?
    return value if value == true || value == false

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be true or false")
    default
  end
end

  def boolean_value(value, default, label)
    return default if value.nil?
    return value if value == true || value == false

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be true or false")
    default
  end
end

# Prepares Quizzy and runs it in production mode in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything lives under storage/ (SQLite databases). Nothing here talks to the network:
# gems are already installed, and assets are served by Propshaft straight from app/assets.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

fail() {
  echo "bin/serve: $*" >&2

}

[ -n "${SECRET_KEY_BASE:-}" ] || fail "SECRET_KEY_BASE must be set"
[ -n "${QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME:-}" ] || fail "QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME must be set"

bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
# A pid file left behind by a killed server would otherwise block the next start.
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare

default: &default
  adapter: sqlite3
  max_connections: <%= ENV.fetch("RAILS_MAX_THREADS") { 5 } %>
  timeout: 5000

development:
  <<: *default
  database: storage/development.sqlite3

# Warning: The database defined as "test" will be erased and
# re-generated from your development database when you run "rake".
# Do not set this db to the same as development or production.
test:
  <<: *default
  database: storage/test.sqlite3

# Store production database in the storage/ directory, which by default
# is mounted as a persistent Docker volume in config/deploy.yml.
production:
  primary:
    <<: *default
    database: storage/production.sqlite3
  cache:
    <<: *default
    database: storage/production_cache.sqlite3
    migrations_paths: db/cache_migrate
  queue:
    <<: *default
    database: storage/production_queue.sqlite3
    migrations_paths: db/queue_migrate
  cable:
    <<: *default
    database: storage/production_cable.sqlite3
    migrations_paths: db/cable_migrate

# Async adapter only works within the same process, so for manually triggering cable updates from a console,
# and seeing results in the browser, you must do so from the web console (running inside the dev process),
# not a terminal started via bin/rails console! Add "console" to any action or any ERB template view
# to make the web console appear.
development:
  adapter: async

test:
  adapter: test

production:
  adapter: solid_cable
  connects_to:
    database:
      writing: cable
  polling_interval: 0.1.seconds
  message_retention: 1.day
  writer_batch_size: 4
  writer_batch_delay: 0.001.seconds

require "application_system_test_case"

# A whole game in the browser: the moderator's big screen and two phones, each in its own browser
# session (so its own cookies and its own player). Changes must show up without a reload.
class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  test "the big screen and the phones follow a game live" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_live_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text
    assert_match %r{/play/[2-9A-HJKMNP-Z]{5}\z}, join_url
    page.execute_script("window.screenMarker = 'same page'")

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_live_text "Hi, Alice!"
      assert_text "Waiting for the quiz to start"
    end
    assert_live_text "Players: 1"

    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_live_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    assert_live_text "Players: 2"
    assert_no_text "Question 1 of"

    click_on "Start"
    assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_live_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    assert_no_text "Correct"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
      click_button "418"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "418"
      click_button "429"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "429"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "Your answer"
      assert_no_selector "button.is-picked", text: "418"
    end
    assert_live_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    click_on "Finish"
    assert_live_text "Correct"
    assert_selector "li.stage-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Correct!"
      assert_selector ".play-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_live_text "No answer"
    end

    click_on "Next"
    assert_live_text "Question 2 of 2"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 2 of 2"
      click_button "WebSocket"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "WebSocket"
    end
    assert_live_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    click_on "Finish"
    assert_live_text "Correct"
    click_on "End quiz"
    assert_live_text "The quiz is over"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_text "Your score: 2 of 2"
    end

    assert_equal "same page", page.evaluate_script("window.screenMarker"), "the big screen never reloaded"
  end

  test "a change still reaches the big screen and the phones when the live pokes are lost" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

    # Lose every poke: only the regular checks of the pages can bring the changes in.
    without_pokes do
      Capybara.using_session(:carol) do
        visit join_url
        fill_in "Your name", with: "Carol"
        click_on "Join"
        assert_text "Hi, Carol!"
      end
      using_wait_time(8) { assert_text "Players: 1" }
    end
  end

  test "a name typed on the phone is kept when the page refreshes" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

    Capybara.using_session(:dana) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Dana"
      # Marks this input, so that it can be told apart from the one the refresh draws.
      page.execute_script("document.getElementById('player_name').dataset.before = 'yes'")
    end

    # Starting the game changes the join page, so the phone redraws its region.
    click_on "Start"
    Capybara.using_session(:dana) do
      assert_no_selector "#player_name[data-before]"
      assert_field "Your name", with: "Dana"
      assert_equal "player_name", page.evaluate_script("document.activeElement.id")
    end
  end

  test "a step whose request fails can be tried again" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    assert_live_text "Players: 0"

    # Only the POSTs fail, as they do on a dropped connection.
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.realFetch = window.fetch;
      window.fetch = (url, options) => (options && options.method === "POST")
        ? Promise.reject(new TypeError("offline")) : window.realFetch(url, options);
    JS
    click_on "Start"
    assert_button "Start"
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    page.execute_script("window.fetch = window.realFetch")
    click_on "Start"
    assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
  end

  private

  # Pokes arrive within about a second. The pages also check on their own every 2-3 seconds, so
  # a longer wait would pass even without the live push.
  def assert_live_text(text)
    using_wait_time(1.5) { assert_text(text) }
  end

  # Makes the server send no pokes for the duration of the block.
  def without_pokes
    original = Turbo::StreamsChannel.method(:broadcast_action_to)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to) { |*, **| nil }
    yield
  ensure
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.define_singleton_method(:broadcast_action_to, original)
  end
end
"

    alice = join_as("Alice")
    bob = join_as("Bob")
    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    bob.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "418").id }
    @game.finish_question!

    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select ".play-status--right", text: "Correct!"
    alice.assert_select "button", count: 0
    alice.assert_select ".play-option.is-correct", text: /429/
    alice.assert_select ".play-option.is-picked .play-option__mark", text: "Your answer"

    bob.get play_path(@game.code)
    bob.assert_select ".play-status--wrong", text: "Wrong!"

    carol = join_as("Carol")
    carol.get play_path(@game.code)
    carol.assert_select ".play-status--neutral", text: "No answer"
  end

  test "the next question replaces the result, and the end shows the score" do
    @game.start!
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.post play_answers_path(@game.code), params: { option_id: option(1, "429").id }
    @game.finish_question!
    @game.next_question!

    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select ".play-question__num", text: "Question 2 of 2"
    alice.assert_select "button[name=option_id]", count: 2

    @game.finish_question!
    @game.end_quiz!
    alice.get play_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_select "h1", text: "The quiz is over"
    alice.assert_select ".result-card__score", text: "Your score: 1 of 2"
  end

  test "the phone's live fragment answers 304 until its own state changes" do
    alice = join_as("Alice")
    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code)
    alice.assert_response :ok
    etag = alice.response.headers["ETag"]

    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code), headers: { "If-None-Match" => etag }
    alice.assert_response :not_modified

    @game.start!
    alice.get play_live_path(@game.code), headers: { "If-None-Match" => etag }
    alice.assert_response :ok, "a new question changes every phone"
    assert_no_match(/<html/, alice.response.body)
    alice.assert_select "#live[data-live-etag-value=?]", alice.response.headers["ETag"]
  end

  test "an unknown join link is not found" do
    get "/play/NOPE1"
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "the join code is not case sensitive" do
    get "/play/#{@game.code.downcase}"
    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "the score is not shown to a visitor who never joined" do
    @game.end_quiz!
    get play_path(@game.code)
    assert_select ".result-card__score", count: 0
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class AnswerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    quiz = create_quiz("Talk", questions: [
      [ "One?", [ [ "a", true ], [ "b", false ] ] ],
      [ "Two?", [ [ "c", false ], [ "d", true ] ] ]
    ])
    @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    @game.start!
    @game.reload
    @player = @game.join("Alice")
    @first_question, @second_question = @game.game_questions.to_a
  end

  test "an answer must pick an option of its own question" do
    answer = Answer.new(player: @player, game_question: @first_question, game_option: @second_question.game_options.first)

    refute answer.valid?
    assert_includes answer.errors[:game_option], "is not an option of this question"
  end

  test "an answer must belong to a question of the player's game" do
    other = Game.create_from_quiz!(@game.quiz)
    answer = Answer.new(player: @player, game_question: other.game_questions.first, game_option: other.game_questions.first.game_options.first)

    refute answer.valid?
    assert_includes answer.errors[:game_question], "is not part of this player's game"
  end

  test "one answer per player and question" do
    option = @first_question.game_options.first
    Answer.create!(player: @player, game_question: @first_question, game_option: option)

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique) do
      Answer.create!(player: @player, game_question: @first_question, game_option: option)
    end
  end

  test "a player's name is stripped and tokens are unique and secret-looking" do
    bob = @game.join("  Bob ")
    assert_equal "Bob", bob.name
    assert_operator bob.token.length, :>=, 30
    refute_equal @player.token, bob.token
  end
end

# Latency probe against the running production server. Not part of the repo.
require "capybara"
require "capybara/cuprite"
require "base64"

Capybara.app_host = ENV.fetch("BASE", "http://127.0.0.1:3000")
Capybara.run_server = false
Capybara.default_max_wait_time = 10

%i[mod p1 p2].each do |name|
  Capybara.register_driver(name) do |app|
    Capybara::Cuprite::Driver.new(app, browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true,
      window_size: [ 1000, 900 ], browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil },
      timeout: 20, process_timeout: 60)
  end
end

auth = "Basic " + Base64.strict_encode64("mod:secret-pass")
def wait_for(session, text, t0)
  deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 10
  loop do
    return (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0) if session.has_text?(text, wait: 0)
    raise "timeout waiting for #{text}" if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
    sleep 0.005
  end
end

mod = Capybara::Session.new(:mod)
mod.driver.browser.headers.set("Authorization" => auth) rescue nil
mod.visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{ENV.fetch('QUIZ', '1')}"
mod.click_on "Start a game"
join = mod.find(".lobby__url").text
puts "join: #{join}"
phones = %i[p1 p2].map do |drv|
  s = Capybara::Session.new(drv)
  s.visit join.sub(%r{\Ahttps?://[^/]+}, Capybara.app_host)
  s.fill_in "Your name", with: drv.to_s
  s.click_on "Join"
  s.assert_text "Hi, #{drv}!"
  s
end
mod.assert_text "Players: 2"

3.times do |round|
  t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  mod.click_on(round.zero? ? "Start" : "Next")
  label = "Question #{round + 1} of"
  mod_ms = wait_for(mod, label, t0) * 1000
  phone_ms = phones.map { |s| (wait_for(s, label, t0) * 1000).round }
  puts "open Q#{round + 1}: screen #{mod_ms.round}ms phones #{phone_ms.inspect} ms"
  phones.first.click_button("ANSWER_PLACEHOLDER") rescue nil
  phones.each { |s| s.all("button[name=option_id]").first&.click }
  sleep 0.3
  t1 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  mod.click_on "Finish"
  c = phones.map { |s| (wait_for(s, "Correct", t1) * 1000).round rescue nil }
  puts "close Q#{round + 1} phones show result after #{c.inspect} ms"
end
t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
mod.click_on "End quiz"
puts "end quiz: phones #{phones.map { |s| (wait_for(s, 'The quiz is over', t0) * 1000).round }.inspect} ms"
EOF

cd /app && cat > app/models/leaderboard.rb <<'EOF'
# The standings of one game: every player, best first.
#
# Points: one per correct pick on a closed question (see `Player#score`).
# Speed: the total time of a player's correct picks. Each pick's time runs from the moment its
# question opened to the player's last pick on it. Equal points: the lower total wins.
# Players still level keep their join order.
#
# A place is a position in that order (1 is first), so no two players share one.
#
# Winners are chosen from this order (see `top` and `draw`). Players with no points never win.
class Leaderboard
  Standing = Data.define(:place, :player, :points, :seconds)

  attr_reader :game

  def initialize(game)
    @game = game
  end

  # One standing per player, in leaderboard order.
  def standings
    @standings ||= rank.each_with_index.map do |(player, points, seconds), index|
      Standing.new(place: index + 1, player: player, points: points, seconds: seconds)
    end
  end

  def size
    standings.size
  end

  def standing_for(player)
    standings.find { |standing| standing.player.id == player.id }
  end

  # "Top N": the first N players of the leaderboard, leaving out players without points.
  # Fewer than N players with points means all of them win.
  def top(count)
    scoring.first(count).map(&:player)
  end

  # "Draw": every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at
  # random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed does not matter here).
  # Players without points never win, so if fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
  def draw(count, random: Random.new)
    return scoring.map(&:player) if scoring.size <= count

    nth_points = standings[count - 1].points
    above = scoring.select { |standing| standing.points > nth_points }
    tied = scoring.select { |standing| standing.points == nth_points }
    above.map(&:player) + tied.map(&:player).sample(count - above.size, random: random)
  end

  private

  # The standings that have at least one point: the top of the leaderboard.
  def scoring
    standings.select { |standing| standing.points.positive? }
  end

  # [player, points, seconds] for every player, best first.
  def rank
    points = Hash.new(0)
    seconds = Hash.new(0.0)
    correct_picks.each do |player_id, game_question_id, picked_at|
      points[player_id] += 1
      seconds[player_id] += picked_at - opened_at_by_question[game_question_id]
    end

    players = Player.where(game_id: game.id).order(:id).to_a
    players
      .map { |player| [ player, points[player.id], seconds[player.id] ] }
      .sort_by { |player, count, total| [ -count, total, player.id ] }
  end

  # The moments the closed questions of the game opened, by game question id.
  def opened_at_by_question
    @opened_at_by_question ||= game.game_questions.where.not(closed_at: nil).pluck(:id, :opened_at).to_h
  end

  # [player_id, game_question_id, picked_at] for every correct pick on a closed question.
  def correct_picks
    Answer.joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_question_id: opened_at_by_question.keys, game_options: { correct: true })
      .pluck(:player_id, :game_question_id, :picked_at)
  end
end
EOF

# A player's pick for one game question. There is at most one per player and question: a new pick
# replaces the old one, and `picked_at` moves to the new pick.
class Answer < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :player
  belongs_to :game_question
  belongs_to :game_option

  before_validation :stamp_pick, if: -> { picked_at.nil? }

  validates :picked_at, presence: true
  validate :option_belongs_to_question
  validate :question_belongs_to_players_game

  def correct?
    game_option.correct?
  end

  private

  # Saved with the pick. Callers that record a new pick set `picked_at` themselves.
  def stamp_pick
    self.picked_at = Time.current
  end

  def option_belongs_to_question
    errors.add(:game_option, "is not an option of this question") if game_option && game_option.game_question_id != game_question_id
  end

  def question_belongs_to_players_game
    errors.add(:game_question, "is not part of this player's game") if player && game_question && game_question.game_id != player.game_id
  end
end
EOF

# One run of a quiz. The game keeps its own copy of the quiz's active questions and their options
# (see `create_from_quiz!`), so editing or deactivating questions never changes a game that is
# running or was played.
#
# Phases:
#   lobby    players join, nothing is open yet
#   open     the current question takes answers
#   closed   the current question is closed and its results are shown
#   finished the game is over: no more joins, no more answers; the leaderboard and winners follow
#
# Every phase change and every change of winners bumps `revision`, and tells the screens and phones
# to reload (see `announce`).
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[ lobby open closed finished ].freeze
  # Join codes avoid look-alike characters (no 0, O, 1, I, L), so they can be read out loud.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[ 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z ].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, length: { is: CODE_LENGTH }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :revision, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }
  validates :winner_count, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Copies the quiz's active questions, in quiz order, with their options, and the quiz's number of
  # winners. Inactive questions are left out, so a game skips them.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz, winner_count: quiz.winner_count)
      quiz.active_questions.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(text: question.text, position: position)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.game_options.create!(text: option.text, correct: option.correct?, position: option_position)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def finished? = phase == "finished"

  def question_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return if current_position.nil?

    game_questions.find_by(position: current_position)
  end

  # Questions that were closed, in order: the ones a player's score is counted over.
  def played_question_count
    game_questions.where.not(closed_at: nil).count
  end

  # Moderator transitions. Each returns true when it changed the game, false when the phase did
  # not allow it (for example, a second click on "Next").
  def start!
    transition do
      next false unless lobby? && game_questions.exists?

      open_question_at!(1)
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    transition do
      next false unless open?

      close_current_question!
      update!(phase: "closed")
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    transition do
      next false unless closed? && current_position < question_count

      open_question_at!(current_position + 1)
    end
  end

  # Ends the game from any phase before "finished". A question that is still open is closed too.
  def end_quiz!
    transition do
      next false if finished?

      close_current_question! if open?
      update!(phase: "finished", finished_at: Time.current)
    end
  end

  # The standings: every player, best first (see Leaderboard). Read fresh each time: not cached.
  def leaderboard
    Leaderboard.new(self)
  end

  def winners
    players.where(winner: true)
  end

  # Winners are picked once the quiz is over. Each returns true when it picked the winners (a draw
  # always picks again, so every click counts), false when the game refuses it.
  def pick_top_winners!
    pick_winners { |board| board.top(winner_count) }
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: Random.new)
    pick_winners { |board| board.draw(winner_count, random: random) }
  end

  # Removes every winner. False when there are none, or the quiz is not over.
  def reset_winners!
    transition do
      next false unless finished? && winners.exists?

      mark_winners([])
      true
    end
  end

  # A player joins. Returns the player, or nil when the game is over. A bad name comes back as an
  # unsaved player with errors.
  def join(name)
    return nil if finished?

    player = Player.new(game: self, name: name)
    announce(:screen) if player.save
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the current question. The last pick counts.
  # Returns :recorded, or the reason it was refused.
  def record_answer(player, option_id)
    return :not_joined unless player&.game_id == id

    question = current_question
    return :closed unless open? && question

    option = question.game_options.find_by(id: option_id)
    return :unknown_option if option.nil?

    save_answer(player, question, option)
    announce(:screen)
    :recorded
  end

  # What the moderator's screen shows. A change in any of these reloads it.
  def screen_fingerprint
    [ revision, phase, players.count, answered_count ]
  end

  # What a player's page shows.
  def player_fingerprint(player)
    answer = player && current_question && player.answers.find_by(game_question: current_question)
    [ revision, phase, player&.id, answer&.game_option_id, answer&.updated_at&.to_f ]
  end

  def answered_count
    question = current_question
    question ? question.answers.count : 0
  end

  private

  # The live pages subscribe to two streams. Pokes carry no data: the pages fetch their own
  # state, so no page ever gets another player's answer or the correct answers early.
  def announce(channel)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_action_to(self, channel, action: :quizzy_refresh, render: false)
  rescue StandardError => error
    # The change is saved already. The pages poll as well, so a lost poke only delays the update.
    Rails.logger.warn("Live poke for game #{code} failed: #{error.class}: #{error.message}")
  end

  def assign_code
    self.code ||= loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      break candidate unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  # Runs the block under a row lock, bumps the revision when it returns truthy, and reloads the
  # screens after the commit.
  def transition
    changed = with_lock do
      result = yield
      if result
        self.revision += 1
        save!
      end
      result
    end
    if changed
      announce(:screen)
      announce(:players)
    end
    changed
  end

  # Picks the winners the block returns (from the leaderboard), once the quiz is over.
  def pick_winners
    transition do
      next false unless finished?

      mark_winners(yield(leaderboard))
      true
    end
  end

  # Only these players are winners from now on. Runs inside `transition`.
  def mark_winners(chosen)
    Player.where(game_id: id).update_all(winner: false)
    Player.where(id: chosen.map(&:id)).update_all(winner: true) if chosen.any?
  end

  def open_question_at!(position)
    game_questions.find_by!(position: position).update!(opened_at: Time.current, closed_at: nil)
    update!(phase: "open", current_position: position)
  end

  def close_current_question!
    current_question&.update!(closed_at: Time.current)
  end

  def save_answer(player, question, option)
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
    answer.update!(game_option: option, picked_at: Time.current)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Two requests from the same player raced to create the answer. The second one updates it.
    retry
  end
end
EOF

module Moderate
  # The moderator's side of a game: the big screen, and the steps that move it along.
  class GamesController < BaseController
    include LiveRegion

    # The steps that pick winners. A pick that finds nobody with points says so on the screen.
    PICK_STEPS = %i[pick_top_winners! draw_winners!].freeze

    layout "screen", only: %i[show]

    before_action :set_game, except: :create
    before_action :set_live_etag, only: %i[show live]

    # "Start a game": a new game of the quiz, opened on its big screen.
    def create
      game = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id]))
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(game), status: :see_other
    end

    def show
    end

    def live
      render_live_fragment(@live_etag)
    end

    def start
      advance(:start!)
    end

    def finish
      advance(:finish_question!)
    end

    def next_question
      advance(:next_question!)
    end

    def end_quiz
      advance(:end_quiz!)
    end

    def top_winners
      advance(:pick_top_winners!)
    end

    def draw_winners
      advance(:draw_winners!)
    end

    def reset_winners
      advance(:reset_winners!)
    end

    private

    def set_game
      @game = Game.includes(:quiz).find(params[:id])
    end

    def set_live_etag
      @live_etag = live_etag(@game.screen_fingerprint)
    end

    # Runs one step. A step the phase does not allow changes nothing, and the screen says why.
    def advance(step)
      if @game.public_send(step)
        flash[:notice] = "Nobody has points, so nobody wins." if PICK_STEPS.include?(step) && @game.winners.none?
      else
        flash[:alert] = refusal_for(step)
      end
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(@game), status: :see_other
    end

    def refusal_for(step)
      case step
      when :pick_top_winners!, :draw_winners!
        "Winners can be picked once the quiz is over."
      when :reset_winners!
        "There are no winners to reset."
      when :start!, :finish_question!, :next_question!, :end_quiz!
        refusal_for_moderation(step)
      end
    end

    def refusal_for_moderation(step)
      return "The quiz is over." if @game.finished?

      case step
      when :start!
        @game.game_questions.exists? ? "The game has already started." : "Add an active question to the quiz before starting."
      when :finish_question!
        "Only an open question can be finished."
      when :next_question!
        @game.open? ? "Finish the question first." : "There are no more questions. End the quiz instead."
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

      if @quiz.update(quiz_params)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), notice: "Quiz saved.", status: :see_other
      else
        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def destroy
      @quiz.destroy!
      redirect_to moderate_quizzes_path, notice: "Quiz deleted.", status: :see_other
    end

    def preview
      @preview = QuizPreview.new(@quiz, answers: params[:answers], pick: params[:pick])
    end

    # The quiz as JSON, ready to copy into "Import quiz" (here or on another Quizzy).
    def export
      @json = JSON.pretty_generate(@quiz.export_data)
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:id])
    end

    def quiz_params
      params.require(:quiz).permit(:title, :winner_count)
    end
  end
end

module GamesHelper
  QR_QUIET_ZONE = 4

  # A button that moves the big screen along. It is part of the live region: the form is sent in
  # the background and the screen redraws from the answer.
  def game_step_button(label, path, variant: "btn--pink")
    button_to label, path, method: :post, class: "btn #{variant} btn--lg",
      form: { data: { turbo: false, live_form: true } }
  end

  # The join link as a QR code: one inline SVG path in a 4-module quiet zone, scaled by CSS.
  # The markup is built from numbers only, so it is safe to mark as HTML.
  def join_qr_svg(url)
    qrcode = RQRCode::QRCode.new(url)
    size = qrcode.modules.size + 2 * QR_QUIET_ZONE
    modules = qrcode.as_svg(standalone: false, use_path: true, module_size: 1,
      offset: QR_QUIET_ZONE, color: "0d0640", shape_rendering: "crispEdges")
    svg = %(<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 #{size} #{size}" ) +
      %(shape-rendering="crispEdges" focusable="false">#{modules}</svg>)
    svg.html_safe
  end
end

require "test_helper"

# Points, speed and winners. Times are set exactly with travel_to: a question opens at its slot in
# the timeline, and each pick is made a given number of seconds after that.
class LeaderboardTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  T0 = Time.zone.local(2026, 11, 19, 10, 0, 0)
  GAP = 100 # seconds between the openings of two questions

  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Talk", questions: [
      [ "Q1", [ [ "wrong", false ], [ "right", true ] ] ],
      [ "Q2", [ [ "wrong", false ], [ "right", true ] ] ],
      [ "Q3", [ [ "wrong", false ], [ "right", true ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  # Plays a game. `picks` maps each player's name to one list per question, in order. Each list holds
  # picks as [seconds after the question opened, correct?]; a later pick replaces an earlier one.
  # Players join in the order of the hash.
  def play(picks)
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    players = picks.keys.index_with { |name| game.join(name) }
    question_count = game.question_count

    question_count.times do |index|
      opened = T0 + index * GAP
      travel_to(opened) { index.zero? ? game.start! : game.next_question! }

      picks.each do |name, per_question|
        Array(per_question[index]).each do |seconds, correct|
          travel_to(opened + seconds) do
            option = game.game_questions.find_by!(position: index + 1).game_options.find_by!(correct: correct)
            assert_equal :recorded, game.record_answer(players[name], option.id)
          end
        end
      end

      travel_to(opened + GAP - 1) { game.finish_question! }
    end
    travel_to(T0 + question_count * GAP) { game.end_quiz! }
    game.reload
  end

  def names(game)
    game.leaderboard.standings.map { |standing| standing.player.name }
  end

  def points(game)
    game.leaderboard.standings.map(&:points)
  end

  test "each correct pick is one point, and places follow the order" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 10, false ] ] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 10, false ] ], [] ],
      "Cara" => [ [], [], [] ]
    )

    standings = game.leaderboard.standings
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Cara ], standings.map { |standing| standing.player.name }
    assert_equal [ 2, 1, 0 ], standings.map(&:points)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], standings.map(&:place)
  end

  test "players level on points are ranked by the total time of their correct picks" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 20, true ] ], [] ],   # 30 seconds
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 5, true ] ], [ [ 23, true ] ], [] ]       # 28 seconds: quicker, so first
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Bob Alice ], names(game)
    assert_equal [ 2, 2 ], points(game)
    assert_in_delta 28.0, game.leaderboard.standing_for(game.players.find_by(name: "Bob")).seconds
  end

  test "points come before speed: a slower player with more points is ahead" do
    game = play(
      "Slow" => [ [ [ 50, true ] ], [ [ 50, true ] ], [ [ 50, true ] ] ],  # 3 points, 150 seconds
      "Quick" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ]                 # 2 points, 2 seconds
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Slow Quick ], names(game)
  end

  test "a wrong pick costs no time, and only the last pick on a question counts" do
    game = play(
      # Alice's first pick is right and quick, her last pick on Q1 is wrong: no point, no time.
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 2, true ], [ 40, false ] ], [ [ 30, true ] ], [] ],
      # Bob: right, but slower than Alice's Q2 pick would be.
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 60, true ] ], [ [ 60, true ] ], [] ]
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Bob Alice ], names(game), "Alice has one point; Bob has two"
    assert_equal [ 2, 1 ], points(game)

    # Changing the pick later moves the time to the new pick: 2 correct picks of 30 and 90 seconds.
    late = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 5, true ], [ 90, true ] ], [ [ 30, true ] ], [] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 40, true ] ], [ [ 60, true ] ], [] ]
    )
    assert_equal %w[ Bob Alice ], names(late), "Alice's last pick took 90 seconds, Bob's 100 is slower; 90 + 30 = 120 > 40 + 60 = 100"
  end

  test "players level on points and time keep their join order" do
    game = play(
      "Dan" => [ [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 10, true ] ], [] ],
      "Eve" => [ [ [ 10, true ] ], [ [ 10, true ] ], [] ]
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Dan Eve ], names(game)
  end

  test "players without points come last, in join order" do
    game = play(
      "Ann" => [ [], [], [] ],
      "Ben" => [ [ [ 4, true ] ], [], [] ],
      "Cy" => [ [ [ 1, false ] ], [], [] ],
      "Di" => [ [], [], [] ]
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Ben Ann Cy Di ], names(game)
    assert_equal [ 1, 0, 0, 0 ], points(game)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ], game.leaderboard.standings.map(&:place)
  end

  test "top N is the first N players of the leaderboard, leaving out players without points" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ],
      "Cara" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ],
      "Dan" => [ [], [], [] ]
    )
    board = game.leaderboard

    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], board.top(2).map(&:name)
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Cara ], board.top(3).map(&:name)
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob Cara ], board.top(10).map(&:name), "fewer players with points than N: all of them win"
  end

  test "draw: players above the N-th place win, and the rest are drawn among the players level with it" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ] ],  # 3
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ],                # 2
      "Cara" => [ [ [ 2, true ] ], [ [ 2, true ] ], [] ],               # 2
      "Dan" => [ [ [ 3, true ] ], [ [ 3, true ] ], [] ],                # 2
      "Eve" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ]                              # 1
    )
    board = game.leaderboard
    assert_equal [ 3, 2, 2, 2, 1 ], board.standings.map(&:points)

    drawn = (1..60).map do |seed|
      winners = board.draw(2, random: Random.new(seed)).map(&:name)
      assert_equal 2, winners.size
      assert_includes winners, "Alice", "more points than the 2nd place always wins"
      winners.last
    end

    assert_equal %w[ Bob Cara Dan ], drawn.uniq.sort, "every player level with the 2nd place can be drawn"
    assert_not_includes drawn, "Eve"
  end

  test "draw: a player level with the N-th place is drawn, but the players below it are not" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ],
      "Cara" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ]
    )
    winners = game.leaderboard.draw(2, random: Random.new(7)).map(&:name)

    assert_equal [ "Alice" ], winners & [ "Alice" ]
    assert_equal 2, winners.size
    assert_empty winners - %w[ Alice Bob Cara ]
  end

  test "draw: when the N-th place has no points, every player with points wins" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ],
      "Cara" => [ [], [], [] ],
      "Dan" => [ [], [], [] ]
    )

    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], game.leaderboard.draw(3).map(&:name)
    assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], game.leaderboard.draw(4).map(&:name)
  end

  test "draw: a clear leaderboard gives the same winners every time" do
    game = play(
      "Alice" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ] ],
      "Bob" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [ [ 1, true ] ], [] ],
      "Cara" => [ [ [ 1, true ] ], [], [] ]
    )

    5.times do |seed|
      assert_equal %w[ Alice Bob ], game.leaderboard.draw(2, random: Random.new(seed)).map(&:name)
    end
  end

  test "draw: with no players who have points, nobody wins" do
    game = play("Ann" => [ [], [], [] ], "Ben" => [ [], [], [] ])

    assert_empty game.leaderboard.draw(2)
    assert_empty game.leaderboard.top(2)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

# The end of a game: the leaderboard on the big screen, the place and points on each phone, and the
# winners picked by the moderator.
class WinnersTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  def pick(game, name, correct:)
    game.record_answer(game.players.find_by!(name: name), game.current_question.game_options.find_by!(correct: correct).id)
  end

  # Alice 2 points, Bob 1 point, Cara 1 point, Dan none: the quiz is over.
  def finished_game(winner_count: 3)
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    game.update!(winner_count: winner_count)
    %w[ Alice Bob Cara Dan ].each { |name| game.join(name) }
    game.start!
    pick(game, "Alice", correct: true)
    pick(game, "Bob", correct: false)
    pick(game, "Cara", correct: false)
    game.finish_question!
    game.next_question!
    pick(game, "Alice", correct: true)
    pick(game, "Bob", correct: true)
    pick(game, "Cara", correct: true)
    game.end_quiz!
    game
  end

  # A phone that joined `game` under `name`, from its own browser session.
  def phone_for(game, name)
    session = open_session
    session.post play_join_path(game.code), params: { name: name }
    session
  end

  test "the settings form has a Number of winners field, 3 by default, that saves a new number" do
    get new_moderate_quiz_path, headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "label", text: "Number of winners"
    assert_select "input[type=number][name='quiz[winner_count]'][value='3'][min='1'][required]"

    post moderate_quizzes_path, params: { quiz: { title: "Talk", winner_count: 2 } }, headers: moderator_auth
    assert_equal 2, Quiz.find_by!(title: "Talk").winner_count
  end

  test "the number of winners must be at least 1, and the form says so" do
    quiz = create_quiz("Talk")

    patch moderate_quiz_path(quiz), params: { quiz: { title: "Talk", winner_count: 0 } }, headers: moderator_auth
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select ".errors li", text: "Number of winners must be greater than or equal to 1"
    assert_equal 3, quiz.reload.winner_count
  end

  test "the screen has no winner buttons until the quiz is over" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "button", text: "Top 3", count: 0
    assert_select "button", text: "Draw", count: 0
    assert_select "button", text: "Reset winners", count: 0

    game.start!
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "button", text: "Top 3", count: 0
  end

    game = finished_game(winner_count: 2)

    assert_select "nav.screen-controls button", text: "Top 2"
    assert_select "nav.screen-controls button", text: "Draw"
    assert_select "nav.screen-controls button", text: "Reset winners"
    assert_select "form[action=?] button", top_winners_moderate_game_path(game), text: "Top 2"
    assert_select "form[action=?] button", draw_winners_moderate_game_path(game), text: "Draw"
    assert_select "form[action=?] button", reset_winners_moderate_game_path(game), text: "Reset winners"
  end

  test "the leaderboard has one list item per player, in order, with the place, the name and the points" do
    game = finished_game
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth

    assert_select "h1", text: "The quiz is over"
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 4
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(1)", text: /1\s*Alice\s*2 points/
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(2)", text: /2\s*Bob\s*1 point\b/
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(3)", text: /3\s*Cara\s*1 point\b/
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(4)", text: /4\s*Dan\s*0 points/

  test "Draw keeps the players above the N-th place and gives the other winner marks at random" do
    game = finished_game(winner_count: 2)
    post draw_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth

  end

  test "the winner steps are refused while the quiz is running, and say why" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_redirected_to moderate_game_path(game)
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth

    assert_equal 0, game.reload.winners.count
  end

  test "a pick with nobody who has points says that nobody wins" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)

    assert_select ".flash", text: "Nobody has points, so nobody wins."
    assert_equal 0, game.reload.winners.count
  end

  test "each winner step needs the moderator's credentials" do
    game = finished_game
    post top_winners_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized
    post draw_winners_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized
