    post top_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_redirected_to moderate_game_path(game)

    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 3
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(1) .leader__badge", text: "Winner"
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(3) .leader__badge", text: "Winner"
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li:nth-child(4) .leader__badge", count: 0
  end

    post draw_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_redirected_to moderate_game_path(game)

    assert_equal 2, winners.size
    assert_includes winners, "Alice"
    assert_equal 1, (winners & %w[ Bob Cara ]).size, "Bob and Cara are level for the second prize"
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 2
  end

  test "Reset winners removes every Winner mark, and says so when there is nobody to reset" do
    game = finished_game(winner_count: 2)
    post top_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    post reset_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_equal 0, game.reload.winners.count

    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select "ol.leaderboard > li.is-winner", count: 0
    assert_select "li .leader__badge", count: 0

    post reset_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select ".flash", text: "There are no winners to reset."
  end

  test "the winner steps are refused while the quiz is running, and say why" do
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    game.join("Alice")
    game.start!

    post top_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_redirected_to moderate_game_path(game)
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select ".flash--alert", text: "Winners can be picked once the quiz is over."
    assert_equal 0, game.reload.winners.count
  end

    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    game.join("Alice")
    game.end_quiz!

    post draw_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    get moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    assert_select ".flash", text: "Nobody has points, so nobody wins."

    game = finished_game(winner_count: 2)
    post top_winners_moderate_game_path(game), headers: moderator_auth
    alice, bob, dan = @phones.values_at("Alice", "Bob", "Dan")

require "application_system_test_case"

# The prizes in the browser: the number of winners is set in Settings, the game is played on a big
# screen with two phones (each in its own browser session), and the winners show up on the leaderboard
# and on the phones without a reload.
class WinnersFlowTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = create_quiz("Frontend Fest 2026", questions: [
      [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", [ [ "418", false ], [ "429", true ] ] ],
      [ "Which protocol is two-way?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ] ]
    ])
  end

  test "the number of winners is set in Settings and drives the Top button of the next game" do
    visit edit_moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    assert_field "Number of winners", with: "3"
    fill_in "Number of winners", with: "1"
    click_on "Save quiz"
    assert_text "Quiz saved."

    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    click_on "Start"
    click_on "Finish"
    click_on "Next"
    click_on "Finish"
    click_on "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"
    assert_button "Top 1"
  end

  test "winners appear on the leaderboard and on the phones, live, and can be reset" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_on "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    assert_live_text "Players: 2"

    click_on "Start"
    assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
      click_button "429"
      assert_selector "button.is-picked", text: "429"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_live_text "Question 1 of 2"
      click_button "418"
    end
    click_on "Finish"
    click_on "Next"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Question 2 of 2"
      click_button "WebSocket"
    end
    click_on "Finish"
    click_on "End quiz"
    assert_live_text "The quiz is over"

    # Alice has 2 points and Bob none.
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li", count: 2
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:first-child", text: "Alice"
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:first-child", text: "2 points"
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:last-child", text: "Bob"
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:last-child", text: "0 points"
    assert_no_selector "li .leader__badge", text: "Winner"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Place 1 of 2"
      assert_text "2 points"
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_live_text "Place 2 of 2"
      assert_text "0 points"
    end

    # Top 3 has two players with points to pick from: Alice is the only one, as Bob has none.
    click_on "Top 3"
    assert_live_text "Winner"
    assert_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:first-child .leader__badge", text: "Winner"
    assert_no_selector "ol.leaderboard > li:last-child .leader__badge"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "You won!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end

    click_on "Reset winners"
    assert_no_selector "li .leader__badge"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "Place 1 of 2"
      assert_no_text "You won!"
    end

    click_on "Draw"
    assert_live_text "Winner"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_live_text "You won!"
    end
  end

  private

  `leader*`, `winner-banner`, `response-*`).

----
## Data

- `quizzes(title)`, `questions(quiz_id, text, position, active)`, `options(question_id, text, correct, position)`.
- Positions are unique per quiz and only swapped, never renumbered. A new question gets `max + 1`.
- Deleting a quiz or question deletes its options (dependent destroy). Deleting a quiz also deletes
  its games.
- Games (see "Live game"): `games(quiz_id, code, phase, current_position, revision, finished_at)`,
  `game_questions(game_id, position, text, opened_at, closed_at)`, `game_options(game_question_id,
  position, text, correct)`, `players(game_id, name, token)`, `answers(player_id, game_question_id,
  game_option_id)` with one answer per player and question (unique index).

----
### Screens

- Big screen: `layouts/screen`, `cover` background (blue, night when over), the `screen-controls` bar
  at the bottom. Lobby: quiz title, join link as plain text (`http://host/play/CODE`, the same
  host the moderator used), QR code (`join_qr_svg`, one SVG path with a 4-module quiet zone),
  "Players: N".
- Phone: `layouts/play`, one column, big buttons. The top bar shows "Hi, <name>!" once joined.
- Both use the stylesheet's classes (`stage-*`, `lobby*`, `play-*`, `result-card`, `mark`).
- The join link is built from the host the moderator's browser used (`play_url`), as the spec asks.
  On a conference network, open `/moderate` at an address the phones can reach (the laptop's LAN
  address and the `PORT`), or the QR code and the link point at `localhost`, which phones cannot reach.
- A failed poke is logged and the change still stands: the pages poll too.

### Gotchas

- `db/schema.rb` must match the migrations. A schema file that is out of date loads first and hides a new
  migration (the migration is then recorded as run, without its columns). Rebuild from the migration
  files when in doubt.
- A `fetch` from the big screen carries the moderator's Basic credentials once the browser has them.
  The system tests set them as headers, like the rest of the suite.

  built from the state (`LiveRegion#live_etag`), not from the HTML. Otherwise nothing is ever 304.

- In an integration test, `assert_select` reads the test's own last response. To check another phone,
  call `assert_select` on that session (`open_session`).

messages.content: This Rails version starts SQLite transactions with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so every transaction takes the write lock up front. That means I can make a pick atomic with respect to "Finish": check that the question is still open and save the pick inside one locked transaction. Then a pick can never be stored after the question closes, and a late pick can't override an earlier valid one. Since time is now part of the score, that's worth doing.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/record_answer.txt <<'EOF'
  # Records the player's pick for the current question. The last pick counts.
  # Returns :recorded, or the reason it was refused.
  #
  # The phase is checked and the pick saved under the game's lock, so a pick cannot be saved after
  # the moderator has closed the question (the lock is the same one `transition` takes).
  def record_answer(player, option_id)
    return :not_joined unless player&.game_id == id

    result = with_lock do
      question = current_question
      next :closed unless open? && question

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "### Live updates

Two mechanisms, both without page reloads. They cover each other's gaps, which matters on crowded
Wi-Fi (missed messages, sleeping phones, dropped sockets):

1. **Pokes (push).** After a change the server broadcasts a Turbo stream with the custom action
   `quizzy_refresh` (`Game#announce`). Two streams per game: `[game, :screen]` for the big screen,
   `[game, :players]` for phones. Phase changes poke both. Joins and answers poke the screen only,
   so 200 phones answering do not make 200 phones reload. `app/javascript/application.js` registers
   the action; it dispatches a `quizzy:refresh` window event with no data.
2. **Polls (pull).** Every live region (`live` Stimulus controller, `app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
   asks its `live` fragment every 2 s (screen and phone). The fragment carries an ETag over the
   state it shows (`LiveRegion`, `Game#screen_fingerprint`, `Game#player_fingerprint`). Nothing new
   means `304` and no DOM work. Polls also run on `visibilitychange` (phone back in front) and `online`.

Client details that matter:

- A poke refreshes at once. There is no random delay any more: speed decides ties, so every phone must
  get a new question at the same moment. A refresh that is
  already in flight is followed by one more, never more than that.
- Responses are numbered; an older response never overwrites a newer one.
- The region is replaced as a whole (`innerHTML`). Text typed in the region is kept, and focus is
  put back (the name field of the join form must survive a refresh).
- Forms marked `data-live-form` are sent with `fetch`. The server answers with a redirect, and the
  page after the redirect provides the new region. Without JavaScript the same forms just work.
- Answers: the tapped option is marked at once. Only the latest tap is sent while one is in flight:
  "the last pick counts" also holds when requests arrive out of order.
- Steps and join buttons are disabled while their request is in flight, so a double click cannot
  start two steps. Answer buttons stay tappable.
- A failed send (network) triggers a refresh, which shows what the server really has.

Latency in the production check (`bin/serve`, Chromium, two phones, a probe that clicks "Start"):
big screen about 0.17 s, phones 0.19-0.25 s after the click. With the old random 0-400 ms delay the
phones took 0.3-0.5 s. A burst of 200 concurrent `live` fetches takes at most about 0.3 s to serve
(median 0.17 s), so the room does not need the delay. The lost-poke test shows that polls alone still
bring every change in within about 2 seconds.

### Screens
"
}

   `quizzy_refresh` (`Game#announce`). Two streams per game: `[game, :screen]` for the big screen,
   `[game, :players]` for phones. Phase changes poke both. Joins and answers poke the screen only,
   so 200 phones answering do not make 200 phones reload. `app/javascript/application.js` registers
   the action; it dispatches a `quizzy:refresh` window event with no data.
2. **Polls (pull).** Every live region (`live` Stimulus controller, `app/javascript/controllers/live_controller.js`)
   asks its `live` fragment every 2 s (screen and phone). The fragment carries an ETag over the
   state it shows (`LiveRegion`, `Game#screen_fingerprint`, `Game#player_fingerprint`). Nothing new
   means `304` and no DOM work. Polls also run on `visibilitychange` (phone back in front) and `online`.

Client details that matter:

- A poke refreshes at once. There is no random delay any more: speed decides ties, so every phone must
  get a new question at the same moment. A refresh that is
  already in flight is followed by one more, never more than that.
- Responses are numbered; an older response never overwrites a newer one.
- The region is replaced as a whole (`innerHTML`). Text typed in the region is kept, and focus is
  put back (the name field of the join form must survive a refresh).
- Forms marked `data-live-form` are sent with `fetch`. The server answers with a redirect, and the
  page after the redirect provides the new region. Without JavaScript the same forms just work.
- Answers: the tapped option is marked at once. Only the latest tap is sent while one is in flight:
  "the last pick counts" also holds when requests arrive out of order.
- Steps and join buttons are disabled while their request is in flight, so a double click cannot
  start two steps. Answer buttons stay tappable.
- A failed send (network) triggers a refresh, which shows what the server really has.

Latency in the production check (`bin/serve`, Chromium, two phones, a probe that clicks "Start"):
big screen about 0.17 s, phones 0.19-0.25 s after the click. With the old random 0-400 ms delay the
phones took 0.3-0.5 s. A burst of 200 concurrent `live` fetches takes at most about 0.3 s to serve
(median 0.17 s), so the room does not need the delay. The lost-poke test shows that polls alone still
bring every change in within about 2 seconds.

messages.content:
Everything is in place. The Gemfile is unchanged and the gems are satisfied offline. Here is the state of the work before I submit:

**What I built** (on the existing Quizzy app, which already had the moderator area and the live game, despite the "no app yet" note)

- **Settings:** "Number of winners" field (number, min 1, default 3). Each game copies the quiz's value when it starts, the same way it copies questions.
- **Scoring:** one point per correct pick. Ties on points are broken by the total time of correct picks, measured from the question's opening to the player's last pick (`answers.picked_at`, set on every pick). Players still level keep join order. Places are positions in that order.
- **Live timing:** I removed the random 0–400 ms delay on pokes and set both poll fallbacks to 2 s. Measured in production, phones now update about 200 ms after "Start", down from 300–500 ms.
- **After "End quiz":** the big screen shows one `li` per player with the place, name, and points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points"). Phones show "Place P of N", the points, and "You won!" for winners.
- **Winners:** "Top N", "Draw", and "Reset winners" are available only once the game is finished. Top N and Draw skip players with no points. Draw keeps everyone above the N-th place and re-draws the rest among players level with it on each click. Each winner change pokes both the screen and the phones, so badges and banners update live.
- **Race fix:** a pick is now checked and saved under the game's lock, so a pick can't be stored after "Finish" closes its question. Since time now affects scores, this matters.

**Verification**

- 181 unit and integration tests and 16 browser tests pass, including new tests for the ranking, draw rules, winner transitions, the screens, and a browser flow with two phones.
- Rubocop and Brakeman are clean.
- `bin/serve` works from a fresh database and as an upgrade of the earlier one. A live production run confirmed winner pokes reach phones.

**Decisions to review**

- Export and import don't carry the number of winners, because the export format is pinned by existing tests. Imported quizzes get the default 3.
- "Draw" is always visible after the quiz ends, not only when there is a tie.
- Design notes are in `docs/notes.md`, and the README mentions the new end-of-game step.

The changes are in the working tree and are not committed, since the repo's only commit is the mockups. I stopped the server and removed the probe data, so `bin/serve` starts clean.
